title: incident-bot: oncall autodiagnostics and runbook linking enhancements
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve signal-to-noise for oncall engineers by enriching autodiagnostics with runbook linking heuristics and SLO-aware suggestions. This PR implements a new runbook linker that matches incident context (service, metric, error class, recent deploy hash) to the canonical runbook index and surfaces prioritized quicklinks in the incident thread. It also adds heuristics to prefer runbooks that have been recently executed for similar SLO violations and falls back to category-level runbooks when exact matches are weak.

Changes included: consolidated autodiag pipeline into a single async worker; new runbook_linker module with fuzzy-title and metadata scoring; telemetry events for link confidence and sampling; updated oncall message templates to include prioritized quicklinks and a short reason; added Linear wiring for ENG-1987 integration test; unit and e2e tests for matching and template rendering.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement runbook linker and scoring pipeline
- [x] Add telemetry (metrics + traces) for confidence and decision path
- [x] Update oncall message templates and unit tests
- [x] Add integration smoke test exercising SLO match and fallback
- [x] Add changelog and docs snippets for operators

Testing: added unit tests (pkg/autodiag/*_test.go) and an e2e integration that runs against local dev index of runbooks. CI flakiness observed in one job related to environment timing; addressed by increasing timeouts in e2e harness. Rollout: merged behind feature flag `autodiag_v2_runbook_linking` with gradual enablement via org-level config. Rollback: feature flag and quick revert of the single worker deployment.

Notes: This PR touches the autodiag pipeline and message rendering; no changes to storage schema. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups (ENG-2043: expand fallback heuristics, ENG-2120: add runbook edit telemetry).
